mean.name: Mean
mean.description: The arithmetic average of a dataset.
mean.interpretation: Represents the central tendency. Highly sensitive to outliers.

median.name: Median
median.description: The middle value in a sorted dataset.
median.interpretation: Robust measure of central tendency. Useful for skewed distributions.

variance.name: Variance
variance.description: The average of the squared differences from the mean.
variance.interpretation: Measures data dispersion. Large values indicate wide spread.

std_dev.name: Standard Deviation
std_dev.description: The square root of variance, representing average distance from the mean.
std_dev.interpretation: Standardized unit of dispersion, in the same unit as the original data.

skewness.name: Skewness
skewness.description: Measures the asymmetry of the probability distribution.
skewness.interpretation: 0 indicates symmetry. Positive skew (> 0.5) means long right tail. Negative skew (< -0.5) means long left tail.

kurtosis.name: Kurtosis
kurtosis.description: Measures the tailedness of the probability distribution.
kurtosis.interpretation: 3 is mesokurtic (normal). > 3 is leptokurtic (fat tails/heavy outliers). < 3 is platykurtic (thin tails/few outliers).

pearson.name: Pearson Correlation Coefficient
pearson.description: Measures the linear correlation between two numeric variables.
pearson.interpretation: Ranges from -1 to 1. 0 indicates no linear relationship. 1/-1 indicate perfect positive/negative linear relationships.

spearman.name: Spearman Rank Correlation
spearman.description: Measures the monotonic correlation between two numeric or ordinal variables.
spearman.interpretation: Outlier robust. Measures if variables increase together, regardless of whether the relation is linear.

cramers_v.name: Cramer's V
cramers_v.description: Measures the strength of association between two nominal/categorical variables.
cramers_v.interpretation: Ranges from 0 to 1. Close to 0 indicates weak association. Close to 1 indicates very strong association.

anova.name: One-Way ANOVA (F-Test)
anova.description: Tests whether the means of a numeric variable differ significantly across categories of a categorical variable.
anova.interpretation: High F-statistic and low p-value (< 0.05) reject the null hypothesis, indicating significant group differences.
